speaker: Doctor
text:
The patient is a 2-week-old female newborn presenting with increasing jaundice over the last 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g, and is exclusively breastfed.

I have asked 1 question so far. I will now ask my second question.

How is her feeding pattern and stool/urine output? Is she having at least 6 wet diapers and 3-4 stools per day, and are the stools yellow/mustard-colored rather than pale or clay-colored?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. I also have Exclusively breastfed, Brother died 3 months after liver surgery.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The family history of a brother dying after liver surgery is highly concerning for a metabolic disorder like galactosemia or tyrosinemia, rather than benign breast milk jaundice. I need to rule out liver dysfunction immediately.

REQUEST TEST: Total_and_Direct_Bilirubin, Liver_Function_Tests, Urine_Reducing_Substances

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal urine reducing substances and normal liver enzymes make galactosemia and major liver disease less likely. I need to check for hemolysis, which is a common cause of unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia in newborns.

REQUEST TEST: Blood_Type_and_Coombs_Test, CBC_with_Ret

How are her feeding volumes, and has she had any vomiting or lethargy?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal Coombs test and CBC rule out hemolytic disease. Given the normal labs, adequate weight gain, and unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia in a healthy, exclusively breastfed infant, this is consistent with breast milk jaundice.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Breast milk jaundice
